entity.scope_notes: Administrative khet (~9.59 km², pop ~67,388 in 2020) along the Phahonyothin corridor with sharply different subareas (Ari, Saphan Khwai, Sanam Pao, Pradiphat, Samsen Nai). Research-verified: the khet's namesake BTS Phaya Thai + ARL terminus sit in Ratchathewi, just outside the khet (app-polygon check confirms); inside stations are Ari, Sanam Pao, Saphan Khwai + SRT Sam Sen. Green 9's likely basis is the Royal Thai Army compound and other state land (controlled access, not public parkland — inference; 14.8 ha unmapped). Victory Monument's attribution is conflicting (app polygon includes the roundabout; sources place it in Ratchathewi).

selection_context.popularity_method: No citywide popularity measure has been collected. Coverage breadth was measured for batch selection only (2024-11-05..2026-11-07 window, publisher-family dedup, coverage-scan.json); it is a research-selection signal, not a popularity score.
selection_context.selection_rationale: District #4 with broad coverage; district-level counterpart to the pilot's st.ari findings; where the 14.8 ha of mapped parkland actually sit.

claims.text_en: Khet Phaya Thai covers 9.595 km2 and since 26 July 2017 has consisted of exactly two khwaeng: Sam Sen Nai (4.923 km2) and Phaya Thai (4.672 km2); numbers 2-5 of the old khwaeng sequence belong to the area split off to form Ratchathewi district in 1989. Population estimates differ by source and year: 70,238 (2017, EN wiki), 66,212 (Dec 2021, EN wiki), 64,037 (Dec 2023, TH wiki) - a declining trend across published snapshots; the app baseline of ~67,388 (2020) sits within this range.

evidence.paraphrase: Two subdistricts listed (Sam Sen Nai 4.923 km2 / 30,476 pop; Phaya Thai 4.672 km2 / 36,736 pop, Dec 2021); note that subdistricts 2-5 were split off to Ratchathewi; history: created 1966 from Dusit and Bang Kapi, Ratchathewi carved off 1989, eastern areas to Din Daeng 1993.

evidence.paraphrase: Two khwaeng split 26 Jul 2017; Sam Sen Nai 4.923 km2 / 29,479 pop and Phaya Thai 4.672 km2 / 34,558 pop as of Dec 2023; total 9.595 km2 / 64,037.

claims.text_en: BMA's own Greener Bangkok site lists only small, named pocket green spaces for the khet: Suan Rom Suk (@Phaya Thai), Suan Yan Phahonyothin (@Phaya Thai, mouth of Soi Ruammit), Suan Ari Samphan, Suan Phaya Thai Phirom, and Suan Rama VI (@Phaya Thai, opposite Sam Sen Witthayalai school). The largest single named public park, Suan Phaya Thai Phirom, opened 4 September 2011, is about 10 rai (~1.6 ha) on EXAT land between the Si Rat expressway and Khlong Sam Sen near Phramongkutklao - third-party maps put it at 13.77204, 100.53212 and some label it Ratchathewi, so even the district's flagship park sits at the administrative edge. Neither the EN nor TH Wikipedia district article lists any park. The app's 14.8 ha of mapped parkland is therefore best explained as the Army Club/Army Stadium compound plus these expressway/leftover-space pocket parks and institutional grounds, not a network of ordinary public parks; the Ari station-unit gap the pilot found is consistent with Suan Ari (the Public Relations Department garden) sitting at the far end of Soi Ari Samphan, beyond an 800 m station radius.

claims.text_en: Rents: two independent sources bracket the app figures. HipFlat's district page (data as of October 2026; 2,241 condo listings) shows average condo value USD689, USD17/sqm, -1.9% YoY, with per-bedroom averages of USD474 (studio), USD652 (1-bed) and USD1,037 (2-bed); its own THB listing examples run 16,500-22,000 for 1-beds (Rhythm Phahol-Ari 18,000; The Line Pradipat 19,000-22,000) and 24,000 for a 2-bed, with upper-end units (Noble Around Ari 1-bed-plus 35,000). A 2025 Ari guide puts studios at 12,000-20,000, 1-beds at 18,000-30,000 ('sweet spot 22-25k') and 2-beds at 28,000-45,000. Against this, the app's editorial 18,000 (1-bed) is a defensible lower-to-mid Ari figure and 37,000 (2-bed) sits inside the Ari guide range but well above the district-wide portal average; portal samples skew to newer advertised condos and include some adjacent-district projects.

claims.text_en: Healthcare is unusually deep for a district this size: Thai wiki lists Veterans General Hospital, Phyathai Saphan Khwai (formerly Paolo Memorial), Phyathai 2, Wichaiyut and Vimut as in-district hospitals, with Phramongkutklao across the boundary in Ratchathewi. The Saphan Khwai hospital - founded 1972 on a site of over 6 rai - was rebranded from Paolo Memorial Phahonyothin to Phyathai Phahonyothin, announced in May 2024 (trade press; search-surface dates: effective 1 April 2024, official 25 May 2024) as a 50th-anniversary repositioning within the Phyathai-Paolo group.

claims.text_en: District-average scores mask four incompatible daily realities inside 9.6 km2: (1) Ari's quiet cafe sois, (2) Saphan Khwai's wholesale/commercial congestion with official traffic-avoidance advisories, (3) the Vibhavadi-Pradiphat band of Army and other state compounds that hold the district's green but restrict access, and (4) the plain apartment/townhouse grid of Sam Sen Nai-Inthamara. A single 'crowd 3' or 'green 9' cannot describe both Ari and Saphan Khwai; the green 9 is anchored in institutional land rather than public park access; and safety 8 was tested only indirectly - a targeted Thai/English news search for 2024-2026 returned scattered youth-violence and pickpocket items whose location attribution was too unreliable to use.

evidence.paraphrase: Institutional anchors (GSB HQ, ministries listed nearby, Army holdings) plus Saphan Khwai's concentrated population in one district.
Ari sois calm and pricey vs Saphan Khwai 'grittier, more local' - the guide treats them as different worlds within walking distance.
Junction-level avoidance advisories show congestion concentrated at Saphan Khwai, not spread evenly.

limitations: synthesis, not a direct source statement
safety conclusion is an absence-of-evidence result, not evidence of absence

claims.text_en: Recent administrative and infrastructure history: khet created 1966 from Dusit and Bang Kapi parts and named for Phaya Thai Palace; Ratchathewi split off 1989 and Din Daeng 1993; khwaengs reorganized into two (Sam Sen Nai, Phaya Thai) on 26 July 2017. Transit changes: BTS stations 1999; ARL interchange 2010; the SRT halt at Phaya Thai has drawn criticism for neglect as its tracks are handed to the Don Mueang-Suvarnabhumi-U-Tapao high-speed rail project. The Saphan Khwai hospital rebrand (May 2024) and recurring GSB AGM junction closures (Feb 2024, Feb 2025) are the main 2024-2026 changes found; no park opening/closure and no Army-land redevelopment for the Vibhavadi compound were found in 2024-2026 reporting.

temporal_scope.notes: Army-land reuse could change the green picture

evidence.paraphrase: 1966 creation; 1973 Huai Khwang separation; 1989 Ratchathewi; 1993 Din Daeng; named for Phaya Thai Palace built 1909.
Two-khwaeng split 26 July 2017.

Rebrand reported May 2024.

limitations: absence of 2024-2026 park/Army-land news is a search result, not proof of stasis

claims.text_en: Vajiravudh College - sometimes assumed to anchor green space here - is in fact in Dusit district (197 Rajvithi Road), on the far side of the railway boundary, so the district's big-campus green candidates reduce to the Army compound, the PRD garden at Soi Ari Samphan, and the expressway-margin pocket parks. Sam Sen railway station (all SRT trains except Eastern Line pass through toward Hua Lamphong) is the district's other rail asset besides the three BTS stations.

question_answers.notes: Khet Phaya Thai, geocode 1014, postal 10400: two khwaeng only - Sam Sen Nai and Phaya Thai (split of khwaengs 26 Jul 2017; district history 1966, Ratchathewi off 1989, Din Daeng off 1993) [phaya-thai-c01]. Aliases are sub-place names inside the khet: Ari/Soi Ari (Phahonyothin Soi 7 network), Sanam Pao (BTS N4; also the road's original name - a former firing range), Saphan Khwai (BTS N5), Pradiphat (road), Inthamara (sois in Sam Sen Nai), Samsen Nai (khwaeng) [c01, c04, c08, c10]. Stops: BTS Ari, Sanam Pao, Saphan Khwai inside; BTS Phaya Thai + ARL terminus just outside in Ratchathewi - the khet's namesake station is not in the khet [c03]. Corridors: Phahonyothin spine inside; Vibhavadi = eastern boundary (partial); Rama VI crosses the south-east; Samsen canal is the southern/western edge; Si Ayutthaya and Sam Sen roads are outside. Outside places: Victory Monument (Ratchathewi), Phaya Thai Palace (Ratchathewi, Ratchawithi Rd), Chatuchak park cluster north of Khlong Bang Sue [c02, c05].

Ari: daytime cafe-and-street-food quarter in low-rise sois - Soi Ari 1-4 'heart of cafe culture', Ari Samphan quieter/good value, Soi Phahonyothin 7 more local [c08]. Saphan Khwai: dense commercial pole - shops, apartments, Big C, most concentrated population, GSB head office, wholesale/grittier character [c09]. Pradiphat/Sanam Pao: military-residential band, post-1932 officer housing, GI-hotel era, now condo-ifying [c10]. Vibhavadi band: institutional Army/state compounds with controlled-access green [c06]. Experiences are anchored to times: cafe mornings/afternoons in Ari; junction congestion at Saphan Khwai peaks [c09, c12].

What people value: the combination of BTS coverage along Phahonyothin plus calm, walkable side-sois with street food and cafes - the guide's own hierarchy prices Soi Ari 1-4 highest exactly where walkability and cafe density peak; Ari Samphan trades walk time for quiet and value; Saphan Khwai trades polish for price and locality [c08, c09]. Mechanism: arterial (jobs/transit) + soi (calm housing) split lets the district price calmness near transit. Supporting: Villa Market Ari and NANA Coffee Roasters (beside the PRD garden) as anchors of the everyday amenity set [c08].

Deliberate counter-evidence: Phahonyothin rush-hour traffic 'can be brutal'; some sois flood in heavy rain; Ari can 'feel sleepy' at night; only one BTS station in the Ari walkshed and it crowds; 30+ min to Silom/Sathorn [c12]. Saphan Khwai junction is a city-level chokepoint warranting police avoidance advisories (GSB AGM 8 Feb 2025, 06:00-18:00) [c09, c12]. On rents: the 'rising rents' narrative is not confirmed by the data at hand - HipFlat shows district asks -1.9% YoY (Oct 2026); what the evidence supports is a high Ari-vs-district spread, not an increase [c11]. Construction pressure: Pradiphat has already converted to condo development since BTS Saphan Khwai; no 2024-2026 construction-wave source found [c10, c15].

Sourced rhythm fragments only: Ari days run on cafe hours with a quiet evening character ('sleepy if you want constant action') [c08, c12]; Saphan Khwai carries all-day commercial/traffic load, with event-driven spikes (GSB AGM closures 06:00-18:00) and evening-market activity reported in snippets (Phahonyothin 24 evening market) [c09]. Weekday/weekend and seasonal patterns (e.g., cool-season pop-up markets at Suan Ari seen only in snippets) were not verified by body-read sources; no monsoon-specific reporting found beyond the guide's flood warning [c12].

Transit: BTS Ari (N3), Sanam Pao (N4), Saphan Khwai (N5) inside on Phahonyothin; ARL interchange at BTS Phaya Thai one stop south, in Ratchathewi; SRT Sam Sen station inside on the western side [c03]. Walk environment: the guide ranks Soi Ari 1-4 most walkable, Ari Samphan quieter, Soi Phahonyothin 7 local; the Phahonyothin arterial itself is traffic-heavy ('brutal' at rush hour) while value and calm lie one soi deep [c08, c12]. No radius-to-time conversions were made; distances like 'Saphan Khwai side walkable from Ari' and '15 min to Chatuchak Park' come from the guide's own framing [c07 limitations, c09].

Groceries/retail: Big C Saphan Khwai and Villa Market Ari are the sourced anchors, plus GSB HQ banking presence at Saphan Khwai [c08, c09]. Ordinary food: street food on Soi Phahonyothin 7, cafes on Soi Ari 1-4 [c08]. Healthcare: Veterans General Hospital, Phyathai Saphan Khwai (ex-Paolo), Phyathai 2, Wichaiyut, Vimut in-district; Phramongkutklao over the boundary [c13]. Gyms: not separately verified (Army sports facilities exist but access is controlled) [c06]. Named wet markets: NOT FOUND - a dedicated search could not verify any specific wet-market name in the khet (the famous 'Suan Mali' namesake is in Pathum Thani); the app's '8 markets' could not be matched to named venues from reliable sources.

Housing types by subarea: Ari - mid-range condos (Noble Around Ari, Rhythm Phahol-Ari, The Line Pradipat, Ideo Phaholyothin nearby) plus older stock from 12,000 studio level [c11]; Saphan Khwai - apartment blocks and shops with the district's most concentrated population [c09]; Pradiphat - post-BTS condo conversion to upper-middle residential [c10]; Sam Sen Nai/Inthamara - townhouse/apartment grid (Thai wiki lists Soi Inthamara, Suthisarn Winitchai) [c01]. Numbers: HipFlat district-wide (Oct 2026, 2,241 listings, asking): studio USD474, 1-bed USD652, 2-bed USD1,037, USD17/sqm, -1.9% YoY; THB examples 16.5k-35k (1-bed) and 24k (2-bed); Ari guide 2025: studio 12-20k, 1-bed 18-30k (sweet spot 22-25k), 2-bed 28-45k [c11]. Test of app 18,000/37,000: 1-bed figure plausible (low end of Ari sweet spot), 2-bed 37k inside Ari range but above district-wide average - defensible only as an Ari-anchored editorial estimate. Sample characterization: portal asking rents skewed to advertised newer condos, includes adjacent-district projects; signed rents not found; period Oct 2025-Oct 2026 with softening trend [c11].

Where the 14.8 ha sits: dominated by the Royal Thai Army Club/Army Sports Stadium compound on the Vibhavadi edge (195 Vibhavadi Rangsit, Sam Sen Nai) plus Channel 5 and other military plots, with BMA's contribution limited to named pocket parks - Suan Rom Suk, Suan Yan Phahonyothin (Soi Ruammit mouth), Suan Ari Samphan (PRD garden), Suan Phaya Thai Phirom (~10 rai, 2011, expressway margin at Rama VI/Khlong Sam Sen), Suan Rama VI (opposite Sam Sen school) [c06, c07]. Subarea access: Ari gets the PRD garden at the far end of Soi Ari Samphan (beyond an 800 m station radius - consistent with the pilot's station-unit gap) [c07]; Rama VI/Phaya Thai-side blocks get the expressway pocket parks; Saphan Khwai/Inthamara get essentially none of the named BMA parks; everyone else walks north to Chatuchak's parks across the boundary [c02, c07]. Directly addressing green 9: it cannot be grounded in public park access; the only coherent basis is institutional/military green plus pockets - hence flag as misleading at district level [c14].

Conditional fit: Ari - cafe-culture workers, couples and remote workers who want calm near BTS and accept quiet nights and 30+ min cross-town commutes [c08, c12]. Saphan Khwai - budget renters and people working in the wholesale/office cluster (GSB, Big C retail) who can tolerate junction congestion [c09, c12]. Pradiphat/Sanam Pao - those wanting mid-range residential with military-area calm; heritage-sensitive users should note the GI-hotel history is mostly built over [c10]. Inthamara/Sam Sen Nai - value seekers on the quieter eastern grid; families should note the absence of BMA parks nearby [c07, c14]. Poor fit: nightlife-first users, flood-sensitive households on low sois, car commuters using Saphan Khwai junction daily [c12].

Dated changes: 26 Jul 2017 khwaeng reorganization into two [c01]; 23 Aug 2010 ARL interchange (in Ratchathewi) and ongoing SRT halt handover issues to the high-speed rail project [c03, c15]; May 2024 Paolo Memorial Phahonyothin rebranded Phyathai Phahonyothin (reported 20 May 2024; search-surface dates effective 1 Apr / official 25 May) [c13]; Feb 2024 and Feb 2025 GSB AGM junction closures at Saphan Khwai [c09]. Suan Phaya Thai Phirom opened 4 Sep 2011 (last major park event found) [c07]. Not found in 2024-2026 reporting: park openings/closures in the khet, Army Vibhavadi-land redevelopment [c15].

What district averages mask: four incompatible subareas (cafe-residential, wholesale-commercial, institutional, plain residential) inside 9.6 km2; crowd 3 and safety 8 cannot be simultaneously true of Ari and Saphan Khwai in the same sense [c14]. Green 9 basis: Army compound + pocket parks + institutional grounds, not public park access; BMA's own list contains no park above ~10 rai scale; OSM decomposition failed from this environment [c06, c07]. Safety 8 basis: no systematic statistic found; news search returned scattered, poorly-locatable incidents - the score is untested rather than contradicted [c14]. Other outside-the-score items: the namesake BTS/ARL station is not in the khet [c03]; pop figures drift downward across snapshots (70,238 in 2017 to 64,037 in 2023) while the app carries a 2020 mid-point [c01]; app '23 temples' vs EN/TH wiki naming Wat Phai Tan as the district's only temple - likely different counting rules (shrines/churches incl.), unresolved; rent 7 depends on which subarea's stock you sample [c11].

preview.text_en: Phaya Thai is a 9.6 km2 district whose three BTS stations (Ari, Sanam Pao, Saphan Khwai) straddle the Phahonyothin corridor, but the daily experience splits between Ari's low-rise cafe sois, Saphan Khwai's dense commercial blocks, and a Vibhavadi-Pradiphat band of Army and state compounds that holds most of the mapped green. The namesake BTS/ARL station is actually across the boundary in Ratchathewi.

guide_lead.text_en: Phaya Thai khet is best read as three districts in one. Along Phahonyothin, Ari's Soi 1-7 grid pairs mid-rise condos with cafe-filled quiet sois, while Saphan Khwai two stops north concentrates shops, apartments and a junction that police close for major events. Between them, Pradiphat still carries its military-institutional character, and along Vibhavadi the Army Club and stadium occupy the largest green block - land you can see but not freely use. Rents reflect the split: portal asks from the 12,000s in older stock to 35,000+ in Ari's newer buildings.

strengths.text_en: Three BTS stations inside the khet plus the ARL interchange one stop south - the district's core transit promise
Ari's walkable cafe sois one soi off the arterial, with street-food-priced eating on Soi Phahonyothin 7
Deep everyday healthcare: five private/military hospitals in-district plus Phramongkutklao across the boundary
Wide rent ladder (roughly 12,000-45,000 THB asking) letting budget and mid-market renters live within walking distance of the same line

tradeoffs.text_en: Phahonyothin rush-hour congestion and the Saphan Khwai junction chokepoint, which police advise avoiding city-wide on big-event days
Public green is pocket-scale: BMA's named parks here are expressway-margin leftovers of ~1-2 ha, while the big green is restricted military land
Flood exposure on some low sois in heavy rain, per the district guide's own cons list
Evening quiet: the area is cafe-daytime oriented and 'sleepy' after dark for those wanting nightlife
Identity confusion is structural: Phaya Thai Road, BTS Phaya Thai, Phaya Thai Palace and Victory Monument are all outside the khet they appear to name

day_night.text_en: Weekday mornings: school and office flows concentrate on Phahonyothin; Saphan Khwai junction backs up toward the sois
Daytime: Ari's cafes and the PRD garden at the end of Soi Ari Samphan absorb the district's leisure foot traffic
Event days: junction-level closures around GSB head office can cut the crossing for a full day (06:00-18:00 advisories)
Evenings: commercial energy drains; the guide describes Ari as sleepier than Sukhumvit-side districts

within_area_variation.text_en: Ari (Soi Ari 1-7, Ari Samphan): cafe-residential, the guide's most expensive and most walkable band
Saphan Khwai: denser, 'grittier, more local', cheapest stock, district's most concentrated population
Pradiphat-Sanam Pao: military plots between residential conversions; history visible in street fabric
Vibhavadi edge: Army Club/stadium, Channel 5, Veterans' Hospital - green without public access
Sam Sen Nai-Inthamara: plain townhouse/apartment grid, few named amenities, no BMA park on its own streets

conditional_fit.text_en: Fit: cafe-culture workers and remote workers priced out of Thonglor/Asoke who want calm sois near BTS
Fit: budget renters targeting Saphan Khwai's apartment stock who work locally or tolerate junction traffic
Poor fit: nightlife-first residents and anyone whose commute crosses town daily (30+ min to Silom/Sathorn per the guide)
Poor fit: households that need daily park access - the khet's public parks are pocket-scale and unevenly placed
Watch item: monsoon-season flooding on specific low sois; ask street-by-street, not district-wide

uncertainties: Green 9 basis unresolved: the 14.8 ha could not be decomposed (OSM queries blocked); the Army compound is the only candidate large enough, and it is not public parkland [phaya-thai-c06, c07]
Safety 8 untested: no systematic crime statistic found; 2024-2026 news search returned only scattered, poorly-locatable incidents [phaya-thai-c14]
App rent reference sits above district-wide portal averages for 2-beds and at the low end for Ari 1-beds; sample definitions differ (portal listings vs editorial estimate) [phaya-thai-c11]

App counts (23 temples, 8 markets, 1,302 food places) could not be matched to named sources; EN/TH wiki name only Wat Phai Tan as the khet's temple, and no wet market was verifiable [phaya-thai-c01 limitations, Q07]
Suan Phaya Thai Phirom's side of the Ratchathewi boundary is ambiguous between BMA and third-party maps [phaya-thai-c07]
